💫 IMPACT STORY!

Meet Khalil Awadh

"The coming of Invention Education to Kenyatta University has genuinely changed how I see myself as an engineer. It gave me opportunities to showcase my abilities, grow in confidence, and pursue the kind of engineering I am passionate about.

Through IvE-KU, I have participated in three design challenges and was fortunate to receive prizes in all three. My latest achievement has given me the opportunity to represent Kenyatta University at the continental level, driven by my passion for improving maternal and neonatal healthcare. I have also presented my work through poster presentations and participated in the Rice360 SEED Program in Houston, an experience that broadened my perspective on engineering, innovation, and collaboration.

Today, I am pursuing an MSc in Medical Device Innovation at Kenyatta University, a continuation of the journey IvE-KU helped me begin.

IvE-KU did more than give me opportunities. It gave me a voice." ✨ 

Kenyatta University Rice University MedTech Kenyatta University The Lemelson Foundation June Madete Kenneth Iloka PhD. Maryanne Muriuki CAROLINE NG'ANG'A Stacy Awinja , MIEEE Eubrea Mitchy Dr. Muthoni Muchai Salome Njoroge James Wambugu

This week we were glad to host a group of students from Delft University of Technology (Netherlands) 

They came to see what can be made in Kenya today, from 3D printing to injection moulding and other local manufacturing capacities. They also wanted to test a big question: is there a business case for making silicone training phantoms for safer childbirth here?

Their project is a low-cost Vacuum Extraction (VE) training phantom; details here: https://lnkd.in/dmfMw6PS

We had good conversations about:
💡  What our local manufacturers can make now, and where the gaps are
💡  Making realistic training tools affordable for East African hospitals and training institutions
💡  How design, engineering and clinical input can come together to improve maternal and newborn outcomes

Thank you to the TU Delft team for your curiosity and rigour. We look forward to seeing where this goes.

Taking innovation beyond the classroom! 🌍

Learning is most impactful when ideas meet real-world experiences. Our MSc Biomedical Engineering – Medical Device Innovation (MDI) Cohort 2 students recently visited Technical University of Mombasa (TUM) for an outreach engagement.

The visit provided an opportunity to connect, exchange ideas, and engage with the wider academic and innovation community, reinforcing the value of collaboration in advancing biomedical engineering and healthcare innovation.

At Invention Education – Kenyatta University, we believe the next generation of MedTech innovators must learn, connect, and create beyond the classroom.

Kenyatta University Rice University The Lemelson Foundation MedTech Kenyatta University Maryanne Muriuki Anthonius Waka Salome Njoroge Abigael Mwangi CAROLINE NG'ANG'A
#InventionEducation #KenyattaUniversity #MedicalDeviceInnovation #BiomedicalEngineering #MedTechAfrica #AcademicCollaboration

Beyond the prototype: Turning medical innovations into impact.

Invention Education – Kenyatta University was pleased to host Isaiah Okoth, Founder and Executive Director of Xenopia Group Limited, for an insightful industry seminar with our MSc Biomedical Engineering – Medical Device Innovation students.

Drawing on nearly four decades of experience across global technology, healthcare, and entrepreneurship, Mr. Okoth shared valuable lessons on what it takes to move medical technologies beyond the prototype and into the hands of patients.

From understanding the root cause of healthcare challenges and the needs of users to building sustainable business models, securing the right partnerships, and navigating the path to commercialisation, his insights challenged our students to think beyond the technology.

His message was clear: successful innovation is not just about creating a device; it is about building solutions that can be adopted, sustained, and scaled to improve healthcare.

We sincerely thank Mr. Okoth for sharing his experience, practical insights, and encouragement with the next generation of African MedTech innovators.

As part of their industry immersion and visits, our MSc Biomedical Engineering, (MDI) Cohort 2 students visited Revital Healthcare (EPZ) Ltd. to gain exposure to the medical device industry.

The experience offered an opportunity to connect classroom learning with the realities of medical device production and the healthcare innovation ecosystem.

Understanding how medical technologies are developed, produced, and brought closer to the people who need them is an essential part of preparing the next generation of MedTech innovators.

We appreciate Revital Healthcare (EPZ) Ltd. Healthcare for hosting our students and supporting experiential learning.

Invention Education – Kenyatta University was delighted to host Nicholas Ocheing, Group Human Resource Manager at The Elewana Collection Collection, for an engaging session with BME 818 students on Professional Development and Communication.

Drawing on his extensive HR leadership experience, Nicholas shared practical insights on interview strategies, career growth, workplace expectations, and navigating professional opportunities.

A valuable reminder that building a successful career takes more than technical expertise; it also takes the right skills, mindset, and preparation.

We extend our sincere appreciation to Nicholas for sharing his time and expertise with our students.
